description: Dependency updates land without a human. `main` requires no approving review, and every check that decides whether an update is safe — the full test shards, clippy, parity and engine snapshots — runs as the `Landing gate` on the merge-group tree, not on the pull request. A maintainer pressing merge therefore adds no signal that the queue has not already produced, so `automerge` presses it instead.

`platformAutomerge` is what makes that work against a required merge queue: Renovate must not merge the branch through its own API call, it has to hand the pull request to GitHub's native auto-merge, which enqueues an entry. This is Renovate's default and is spelled out because the whole arrangement rests on it.

Two gates deliberately survive. A release still soaks for `minimumReleaseAge` before a pull request exists at all, and the `dependencyDashboardApproval` rules below mean a major or 0.x minor bump opens nothing until a maintainer ticks it — so those are reviewed before they are ever queued, not after.

lockFileMaintenance.description: Workspace builds use --locked, so a stale Cargo.lock is a build input like any other. Renovate gives this object its own default schedule that wins over the repository one, so the weekly cadence is spelled out here rather than inherited.

git-submodules.description: content/ is a deliberately pinned game-data submodule, not a dependency to track.

vulnerabilityAlerts.description: A security fix must reach a pull request immediately, so it overrides everything below: the daily schedule, the week-long release soak, the compatible-update grouping, and the dashboard approval that otherwise holds major and 0.x bumps.

packageRules.description: The whole workspace shares one Cargo.lock, so separate compatible-update pull requests would each invalidate the others. Collect them into one.
Cargo treats a 0.x minor bump as incompatible, so it breaks a build exactly like a major does. Hold those for review rather than folding them into the compatible-update group.
Workflow action bumps are independent of the Rust build; keep them in their own pull request.

This action is pinned to the commit tagged for the exact channel in rust-toolchain.toml. It publishes no semver releases, so Renovate cannot resolve a digest for it, and advancing it independently would desync the CI toolchain from the pinned Rust version.

This engine is held to bit-for-bit parity with the C++ oracle and its CI is currently disabled, so a major bump must not open unreviewed. Tick it on the dependency dashboard to request the pull request.
